There are $3$ columns in $C$ and $3$ rows in $D,$ so $C$ and $D$ are conformable for multiplication:

$$
\underset{\bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{2} \times \color{green}{\fbox{3}}}{C} \underset{\color{green}\checkmark}{\cdot} \underset{{\color{green}\fbox{3}} \times \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{2}}{D} = 
	\underset{\bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{2} \times \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{2}}{CD}
$$

$$

$$

e-5885.worked_solution:
Here, the first factor is a $3 \times 1$ matrix and the second factor is a $1 \times 2$ matrix. 

There is $1$ column in the first matrix and $1$ row in the second matrix, so the product is well defined:

$$
\bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{3} \times {\color{green}\fbox{1}} {\color{green}\checkmark} {\color{green}\fbox{1}} \times \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{2} = 
	\bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{3} \times \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{2}
$$

Computing the product, we have

$$
\eqalign {
    \left\lbrack
    \matrix {
       -1 \
 	0 \
        -2
    }
    \right\rbrack

    \left\lbrack
    \matrix {
        2 & -5
    }
    \right\rbrack

	&= 

    \left\lbrack
    \matrix {
        (-1)\cdot 2 & (-1)\cdot (-5) \
        0\cdot 2 & 0\cdot (-5)\
        (-2)\cdot 2 & (-2)\cdot (-5)
    }
    \right\rbrack \[5pt]

	&=

    \left\lbrack
    \matrix {
       -2 & 5 \
       0 &  0 \
       -4 &  10 
    }
    \right\rbrack 
}
$$

Here, the first factor is $4\times 1$ matrix and the second factor is a $1\times 3$ matrix. 

There is $1$ column in the first matrix and $1$ row in the second matrix, so the product is well defined:

$$
4\times \boxed{\text{1}}✓\boxed{\text{1}}\times 3=4\times 3
$$

Computing the product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4\cdot 1 & 4\cdot 0 & 4\cdot 4 \\ 2\cdot 1 & 2\cdot 0 & 2\cdot 4 \\ 1\cdot 1 & 1\cdot 0 & 1\cdot 4 \\ 1\cdot 1 & 1\cdot 0 & 1\cdot 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 16 \\ 2 & 0 & 8 \\ 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 1 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$

decision.explanation: The 3×1 matrix times the 1×2 matrix gives a 3×2 matrix. Multiplying 0, -2, and -3 by [1, 2] gives rows [0, 0], [-2, -4], and [-3, -6], matching option e.

after.name: Question 14
after.worked_solution:
Here, $A$ is $3\times 1$ matrix and $B$ is a $1\times 2$ matrix. 

There is $1$ column in matrix $A$ and $1$ row in matrix $B$, so the product is well defined:

$$
{A}_{3\times \boxed{\text{1}}}{\cdot }_{✓}{B}_{\boxed{\text{1}}\times 2}={AB}_{3\times 2}
$$

Computing the product, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0\cdot 1 & 0\cdot 2 \\ (-2)\cdot 1 & (-2)\cdot 2 \\ (-3)\cdot 1 & (-3)\cdot 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ -2 & -4 \\ -3 & -6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
